title: Japan is launching a mission to Mars’s largest moon Phobos | New Scientist
description: The Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft, set to launch on 20 October, will bring back samples that should solve a moon mystery that has been vexing scientists for more than a century
author: Leah Crane

title: El Niño has killed hundreds of children in Sudan | New Scientist
description: Drought driven by El Niño is causing hunger and disease in Sudan that has already killed hundreds of children
author: Alec Luhn

title: Scientists have just voted to abolish leap seconds | New Scientist
description: Since 1972, officials have added 27 leap seconds to the universal clock, but in a meeting this week in France they have decided to abandon the practice
author: Jo Marchant

title: Will physics be the next field to be turned upside down by AI? | New Scientist
description: AI has taken huge strides in computer programming and mathematics – physics could be next
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Antarctica’s ‘doomsday’ glacier will keep melting even if oceans cool | New Scientist
description: Computer models suggest that unrealistically cold oceans would be insufficient to stop Thwaites glacier retreating, although a neighbouring glacier might begin to grow
author: Alison George

title: Why a high school in Virginia is getting a quantum computer | New Scientist
description: Starting in January, students attending Skyview High School in Virginia will learn about the building blocks and principles underlying quantum computers by working with one directly
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan
